inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q diluted weighted average (1,975m; basic 1,970m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks ($12.1bn FY25, $5.6bn H1-26, guided $10-20bn/yr) are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat. The July-2025 Hess all-stock issuance ($50.6bn) is already in the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 22: stock-option expense $73m + SARs/restricted stock/performance shares/RSUs $399m = $472m (FY24 $600m, FY23 -$15m). Not XBRL-tagged, so absent from Metrics.csv. The $146m/$145m tagged as PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation (and stored as kpis equity_award_taxes) is the 1% SHARE-REPURCHASE EXCISE TAX per the cash-flow note, not award withholding, so it is not added.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 mid-cycle normalised (Brent $70 deck, full-year Hess)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.9, ERP 5.0% -> CoE ~8.8%; debt ~15% of capital at ~4.8% pre-tax (4.0% post-tax) -> WACC ~8.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios: commodity-price risk is charged in the scenario flows (Brent $60/$70/$80 decks), not by a WACC premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost ($6.0bn liability FY25) already sits inside operating cash costs, so no deduction from flows and operating leases excluded from net debt; finance leases are inside reported total debt (LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations). One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows modelled on consolidated basis; NCI charged once as a bridge deduction at book ($5,675m at 2026-06-30, up from $841m pre-Hess). NCI share of earnings ~$0.45bn/yr, about 2-3% of NI, so book is a fair proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, MID-CYCLE (cyclical commodity producer; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of CVX; no memory entry. WHY MID-CYCLE: the valuation date sits inside a Brent spike (H1-26 avg $92, >$107 in September on the Iran/Hormuz disruption); Q2-26 NI $12.2bn is the highest in six years and is not a repeatable base. Company sensitivity is ~$600m after-tax earnings/cash flow per $1/bbl Brent (Q2-26 10-Q), so the H1-26 run-rate (~$50bn OCF annualised) de-rates to ~$37bn OCF at $70, i.e. ~$18-19bn FCF after $18-21bn guided capex -- consistent with FY24 ($15.0bn at $81 Brent, pre-Hess) and FY25 ($16.6bn at $69, half-year Hess). FY0 revenue $195bn = FY25 $189bn at $69 Brent + full-year Hess + 7-10% guided 2026 production growth, held to a $70 deck. Year-1 owner FCF ~$18.9bn (9.3% margin). The above-deck cash already being earned in H2-2026 is added once in the equity bridge, not capitalised. BALANCE SHEET (10-Q 2026-06-30): cash $8,527m + time deposits $3m = $8,530m; debt = short-term $401m + long-term incl. current and finance leases $36,674m = $37,075m; net debt $28,545m (FY25 10-K: $34,461m). INTEREST INCOME not stripped: CVX is net-debt, and flows are unlevered with net debt deducted. EQUITY AFFILIATES (TCO 50%, CPChem 50%): their cash contribution arrives through OCF as distributions and is inside the FCF base and margin calibration; affiliate capex is outside CVX capex. BUYBACKS: repurchaser (flat count funded, not a convention).

equity_bridge.note: Brent ~$95-107 in Q3/early Q4-26 vs the $70 deck: ~$25/bbl x $0.6bn per $1 x ~0.5yr = ~$7.5bn after tax, haircut to $5.0bn for reversal risk on de-escalation. Counted once here; the projected flows are all on the $70 deck.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: guided 2-3%/yr production growth to 2030 plus modest price inflation on a constant $70 deck. Every trailing CAGR measures the commodity cycle, not the business: FY20 ($42 Brent, COVID) is the 5-yr base, FY22 ($99 Brent) the 3-yr base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6-8%) diverges >30% from revenue (-8% 3yr / +15% 5yr) and EPS (-29% 3yr; FY20 EPS negative). Equity growth is inflated by the July-2025 $50.6bn all-stock Hess issuance. None of the historical CAGRs is usable as a forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported OCF - capex - SBC): FY22 ~$37.1bn, FY23 $19.8bn (SBC -$15m), FY24 $14.4bn, FY25 $16.1bn. FY22 SBC not disclosed in the FY25 10-K three-year window; approximated at ~$0.5bn. SBC is ~0.25-0.3% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs barely differ; the gap is not a signal here.

base.narrative: $70 Brent deck. Guyana (Uaru 2026, further FPSOs), TCO FGP at full rate and Permian plateau deliver the guided 2-3% production CAGR; Hess synergies ($1.5bn realised) and Permian capital efficiency lift EBITDA margin ~1pp; capex sits at the low-to-mid end of $18-21bn.
base.terminal_cap_rationale: Mid-range of the 12-15x cyclical band: the flows are already normalised to a $70 deck, so the bottom of the band would charge cyclicality twice. Gordon at 8%/1.5% is ~15.6x, so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: $80 Brent deck: Hormuz-era underinvestment keeps the mid-cycle higher. Guyana ramps ahead of plan, Venezuela's new terms add low-capital barrels, Project Kilby (2.67 GW Microsoft power campus) reaches FID and seeds a contracted gas-to-power annuity, and capex holds at the $18bn floor.

bear.narrative: $60 Brent deck: Hormuz resolves, OPEC+ spare capacity returns and the spike reverses into oversupply. CPC pipeline disruption through Russia curtails TCO exports, Venezuela's license is pulled again, Guyana (non-operated) slips; refining margins normalise lower and demand erosion from EVs caps terminal growth near zero.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle Chevron at a $70 Brent deck: the Hess deal gives it a 30% Stabroek interest that grows through the decade, TCO's FGP/WPMP run at capacity, and the Permian plateau at ~1.7m boe/d throws off cash at lower capex. Production grows 2-3%/yr, margins gain ~1pp from synergies and efficiency, and ~$19-21bn of annual owner FCF funds the dividend plus mid-range buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: A structurally higher mid-cycle ($80) after the 2026 Hormuz shock exposes a decade of upstream underinvestment, with Chevron's low-breakeven barrels (Permian, Tengiz, Guyana) capturing it. Venezuela's September-2026 terms add barrels without much capital, and the Microsoft/Project Kilby power deal opens a contracted gas-to-power business that supports a higher terminal multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The spike reverses: de-escalation plus OPEC+ spare capacity push Brent to a $60 mid-cycle. Chevron's specific geopolitical concentrations bite together: CPC transit through Russia constrains TCO, OFAC pulls the Venezuela license again, and the Essequibo dispute clouds non-operated Guyana. Refining normalises and energy-transition demand erosion caps terminal growth near zero.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): the valuation date sits on a geopolitical price spike whose reversal is the most likely single path, and CVX carries stacked single-country risks (CPC/Russia, Venezuela OFAC, Essequibo). Base 50%: a $70 deck matches both the company's own planning deck ($60-80 buyback guidance range) and the pre-spike strip. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a higher structural price AND Guyana/Venezuela/Kilby execution, several independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Chevron is valued on mid-cycle owner FCF at a $70 Brent deck, not on the spike-inflated H1-2026 run-rate. The current price discounts something close to the bull deck, so on a through-the-cycle view the stock is pricing in the Hormuz shock persisting. The H2-2026 windfall is credited once in the bridge; it does not justify capitalising spike cash flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Brent deck: each $1/bbl is ~$0.6bn/yr after-tax cash flow, roughly $3-4/share of value over the horizon at 8%; the scenario decks span $60-$80.
Terminal assumptions for a depleting resource base: the 10-12x cap and 1.5% terminal growth assume reserve replacement continues; an energy-transition decline would make terminal growth negative.
Geopolitical concentration: TCO exports via the Russian-transit CPC line, Venezuela OFAC license volatility, the Guyana-Venezuela Essequibo dispute.
Equity-affiliate cash (TCO, CPChem) is only captured as distributed; TCO distribution policy and loan repayments can shift year-to-year cash materially.
The H2-2026 windfall bridge item ($5bn) is an estimate from company sensitivity, not a reported figure.
